notes: Partition checked: all 20 source ids and all 23 target ids appear exactly once, and every head is a member of its array.

*in his stead* is divided with the possessive on the suffix (rule 18) and the discontinuous *in ... stead* on `תַּחַת`, headed on *stead* rather than the connective (rules 24, 25). Fusing all three under rule 30 was available, but that rule's one-rendering condition fails because the ASV spends *his* on the suffix in particular.
The object marker is `unrepresented`: *buried him* spends no word on the object relation, and the English pronoun answers to the suffix (rules 16, 18).
Where the Hebrew writes an explicit subject — `יוֹתָם`, and `אָחָז בְּנוֹ` — the verb keeps only its lexical verb; only `יִּקְבְּרוּ`, which has none, takes the English subject pronoun under rule 17.
